# W01 modular finish r2: independent read-only PBR review

**Verdict: correct. Do not retain.** r2 fixes the two most specific r1 defects: the right side is no longer near black, and the P11 gap can now be read. But the finish swung from too dark to too bright and clean. At every exposed size it reads as a light-gray painted tank with soft gray-and-white blotches, much like urban camouflage. It does not read as a burnt, ash-covered vehicle.

## What I opened
- **r2 (job 00ff9b75… r3, CP ffd4c1b8…):** `render-evidence.json`; all six views at 1000 and 256; left, right, top and rear-three-quarter at 128.
- **Controls, same cameras:**
  - r1: right, left and top at 1000; rear-three-quarter at 1000; right at 128.
  - r0: right, left and top at 1000.
  - Physical-only: right and front at 1000; right at 128.
- **Photos:** `doha-i14.png` and `usmc-hansen.jpg`.
- **Not opened:** the three audit JSONs (native, UV image, normal). Their findings, as you summarised them, stand as separate technical evidence that I haven't checked.
- **Hashes:** I didn't compute any. `render-evidence.json` *reports* identical repeat hashes at all three sizes; I haven't verified that.

## Pixel findings (r2)
- **Value and side reading:** the right side at 1000 is now mid gray instead of near black, and the hull, turret, gun and running gear separate cleanly. The overall value is too high, though. The top view at 1000 is close to off-white across the deck, turret roof and engine deck. The rear-three-quarter is an almost uniform pale gray, with only faint darkening on the skirt.
- **P11 gap:** the dark rectangle between the skirt panels is clearly visible on the right at 1000 and 256. At 128 it is still a small dark notch. I see no invented hole.
- **Hull and Bustle:**
  - **Hull:** visible change. There are soft light and dark masses on the rear upper hull (both sides) and the front glacis.
  - **Bustle:** got lighter compared with r1, but stays an almost flat mid gray on both sides with no char or ash variation I can see. The Bustle field has effectively no visible condition.
- **Continuity at seams and edges:** the turret blotch on the left wraps across the cheek-to-side edge, and the skirt blobs mostly continue across panel seams. That is better than r1's fields stopping at each seam. Some skirt patches still change abruptly at seams on the right (around x≈295), so this is only partly closed. I couldn't confirm it more precisely without cropping, which I didn't do.
- **Burnt and ashy, or paint/camouflage:** this is the main failure. The marks are large, soft-edged, gray/white/charcoal blobs over a clean gray base, which reads as urban or winter camouflage, or airbrushing. There are no hard-edged scorch boundaries, no bleached panels set against black char, and no residual paint islands. The gun, turret roof, bustle and rear deck look untouched.
- **Metal and glass:** muted. The vision blocks are dark gray (r0's blue glass is gone), and the open-hatch interior is dark. No bright metal stands out. Closed.
- **Shading check:** the dark diagonal band on the front glacis is the gun barrel's cast shadow. It is also in the physical-only front render, so it is not a finish defect.
- **Recognizability:** the tank silhouette, open hatch, 29 left shoes and retained running gear read at every size. The finish only helps the condition reading at 1000, and only on the side skirts. At 256 and 128 the vehicle looks like an intact gray tank, apart from the P11 notch.

## Against the photos (category only)
Both photos show hard-edged, high-frequency patterns: black char next to sharply bounded bleached or white panels, rust-brown, and surviving tan or green paint islands. r2's soft, low-frequency blobs in a narrow gray range don't capture that, even allowing that the photos are a general category and not a color map. r1 was too black; r2 overcorrected to too pale and even.

## Prior defects
| r1 defect | r2 status |
|---|---|
| Right side nearly black | **Closed** |
| P11 gap illegible | **Closed** |
| Fire looks uniform or airbrushed | **Remains.** Now reads as pale camouflage blotching |
| Face fields stop at skirt seams | **Partly closed.** Most blobs cross seams; some breaks remain on the right skirt |
| Bright metal and glass | **Closed** (was already improved in r1) |
| *New:* overall value too bright; top, rear and Bustle read clean | **Opened by r2** |

## Strongest concern
The finish's frequency and value structure is wrong. The source category calls for hard-edged char-to-bleach contrast with residual paint. r2 delivers soft gray/white mottling on a bright, uniform base. At 256 and 128 that reads as a camouflaged or primer-gray intact tank, and the top, Bustle and rear deck carry essentially no condition.

The direction for the correction:
- Bring the base value down partway between r1 and r2.
- Use hard-boundary char and bleach masks instead of soft blobs.
- Put visible condition on the Bustle, deck and roof.
- Remove the blob shapes that read as camouflage.

There is no score, approval, formal go, or animation or force claim in this review. The physical source scope (settled static, P11 absent, open hatch, retained running gear) was respected, and I didn't require any hidden damage to show through the armor.
decision: Root and actual Opus reject finish retention: gray camouflage or primer reading with soft clouds. Return to source phase after third local finish candidate.
